# Add Investor staff members

## Problem statement

The staff family has no member that manipulates the **market row** itself: every ability so far buffs income, reputation, costs, incidents or hand capacity. The Investor introduces a market-shaping role — one **free market re-roll per turn** that is **biased toward the business type where the Investor is employed** — giving players a reason to invest coins in scouting favourable offers rather than accepting the first row they see. Moving the Investor to a different business costs an action point, so the ability is a deliberate positioning decision rather than a free upgrade.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a market-manipulation tool that rewards placing an Investor next to the business type they are trying to grow.
- **Main Street player (mid-game)** — wants a coin-free way to dig for a missing synergy piece (e.g. a Food business while running a Food cluster).

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a free market re-roll each turn while an Investor is employed, so that I can look for a better offer without paying the escalating re-roll cost (MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ).
- As a Main Street player, I want the Investor's free re-roll to be 75% likely to surface cards relevant to the business it is employed at, so that placing it near my cluster meaningfully improves my odds.
- As a Main Street player, I want to move the Investor to a different business for one action point, so that I can retarget the bias at a cost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Investor card exists in the catalog.** A new `staff-investor` row is added to `src/card-data.csv` (feature flag `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`, bias `0.75`, no hand slots, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`), with a tier assignment, cost, ongoing cost and description consistent with the staff ladder and the ×100 coin scale; it flows into the general market via the existing tier-gated staff deck (`createStaffDeck`).
- **AC2 — One free re-roll per turn.** While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform **one** coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it **advances the per-turn escalation counter** (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- **AC3 — Relevance bias.** On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a **75% chance** to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`; event `targetSynergy`/effect; staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap with the hosting business's synergy types) — the free `refillSingleRowMarket` path is parameterised so the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- **AC4 — All staff relocation costs an action point.** Relocating a hired staff member from one business to another is exposed as a player action and consumes **1 action point** for **all** staff (the existing `placeStaffOnBusiness` placement is action-free today and must be action-gated when used as a relocation; the initial placement at hire time remains part of the hire action). The move respects `allowedBusinessTypes` and employment-slot capacity, is undoable, and is persisted.
- **AC5 — UI & tooltips.** The market re-roll button/tooltip and the Investor's staff tooltip/employed-staff summary surface (a) whether the free re-roll is still available this turn and (b) the 75% relevance bias; the button label/tooltip reflect the coin-free state when available and the escalated cost when not. Wording stays consistent with the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename if that lands first.
- **AC6 — Undo, save/load and determinism.** The per-turn free-re-roll flag, the per-turn escalation counter it increments (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`), the Investor's location and any bias state participate in undo/redo (`snapshotAction`) and in `MainStreetStateSerialize` (serialize + migrate backfill + deserialize), so mid-turn reload preserves both availability and the escalated next price; the bias draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed ⇒ same-game determinism holds.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit/integration tests cover: catalog + CSV contract; free re-roll is coin-free, once per turn, resets at `WeekStart` and advances the escalation counter; the 75% relevance bias (deterministic with a seeded RNG) and its random fallback; movement action cost + undo + save/load round-trip; and existing re-roll/discount/action-economy tests are updated for the new card and counts.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, the Main Street rules docs (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`) and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC9 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **New mechanic, not just data.** The relevance bias and the free re-roll are new engine behaviour; they must be additive and must not change existing behaviour when no Investor is employed.
- **Single source of truth for re-roll cost.** The free re-roll must not silently bypass `refreshMarketCost()`; the paid path and its escalation (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) remain authoritative for non-free re-rolls, and the free re-roll must increment the same per-turn escalation counter.
- **Reuse the market composition model.** `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`) enforces the ≥1-business row composition; the biased draw must preserve that invariant.
- **Placement/employment invariant.** `business.employedStaff` and `staff.employedAtSlot` are kept in sync by the existing placement helpers; the move action must route through them.
- **Art drift guard.** `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` requires every unique card name to map to dedicated art or a documented pending-art target, and forbids growing the art-less baseline (currently 79). The Investor therefore needs a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite **or** an explicit, producer-approved pending-art entry (see `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`).
- **Coin scale.** All coin values are ×100 (per the integer-economy migration); the Investor's cost/ongoing cost must follow the existing staff ladder (`MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z`).

## Existing state

- **No Investor exists** anywhere in the repo or worklog (searched `investor`, case-insensitive, excluding `node_modules`/`dist`); only the unrelated `Investor Bonanza` event fixture appears in a test.
- **Market re-roll is already action-free** (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 "Free operations: Market re-roll/refresh"), so "without using an action" means the Investor's re-roll is free of **coins** as well; the normal re-roll costs `REFRESH_MARKET_COST` (500, escalating per `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`).
- `refillSingleRowMarket(state)` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) builds the row: 3 slots, ≥1 business, at most 1 upgrade / 1 event / 1 staff, drawing via `state.rng` (seeded).
- `refreshMarket(state)` / `refreshMarketCost(state)` / `canRefreshMarket(state)` live in `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`; discounts come from `refreshCostDiscount` staff and the Negotiator skill.
- **Staff placement is free today**: `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`) explicitly consumes no action/coins; `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand`/`removeStaffFromBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:674/692`) wrap it in `snapshotAction`. There is currently **no** player-facing "move staff" action.
- Staff card fields live in `StaffCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts:330`), parsed in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` (CSV columns incl. `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `allowedBusinessTypes`); the catalog currently holds **25** staff rows.
- Per-turn gates (`peekUsedThisTurn`, `favourUsedThisTurn`, `businessPlacedThisTurn`) are reset in `executeWeekStart` (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`).
- Card-count baselines that will shift when a staff row is added: `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (`toHaveLength(25)`), `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` (166 / 174 totals), `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- **CSV/catalog:** add `staff-investor` with a new bias column (e.g. `marketRelevanceBias = 0.75`) plus a free-re-roll marker (e.g. `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`), no `handSlotsAdded`, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`, and a description in the existing "reduces X by Y" house style.
- **Types/parsing:** add the new optional `StaffCard` fields and parse them in `MainStreetCardsTemplates` (numeric column for the bias; boolean/flag column for the ability).
- **Engine:** add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` state (reset at `WeekStart`), a `canUseFreeMarketReroll`/`useFreeMarketReroll` pair (coin-free, action-free, once per turn) that **increments `marketRefreshesThisTurn`**, and a `refillSingleRowMarket`-compatible biased draw parameterised by the hosting business's synergy types + `0.75`.
- **Movement:** add a move-staff engine function + command that charges 1 action via the existing weekly action budget for **any** staff relocation, reusing `placeStaffOnBusiness` semantics (adding the action gate at the command layer).
- **Serialization:** add the new state field to serialize, migrate (backfill `false`/`0`) and deserialize.
- **UI:** market re-roll button/tooltip shows the free re-roll availability; staff tooltip/employed-staff summary states the free re-roll + 75% bias; a move-staff affordance that costs an action.
- **Docs & art:** update the rules/catalog/progression docs; add the Investor sprite (or a documented pending-art entry) and regenerate `card-art-map.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `staff-investor` row (new bias column + free-re-roll flag; tier, cost, ongoing cost, description).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard.freeMarketRerollPerTurn?` / `StaffCard.marketRelevanceBias?` (+ doc comments).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the new CSV columns into the new fields.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — free re-roll path (`canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`), bias-aware `refreshMarket` variant, and cost/label reporting.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — parameterise `refillSingleRowMarket` with an optional relevance pool; keep the default path unchanged.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the per-turn free-re-roll flag.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — new per-turn state field (and serialized-state entry).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialize, migrate backfill (and deserialize) the new field.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — move-staff engine function + command (1 action), free-re-roll command.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — helpers to detect the employed Investor and its hosting business synergy types.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — free-re-roll button state, tooltip and availability text.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — employed-staff summary / staff tooltip line for the new ability.
- `src/card-art-map.json`, `src/sprites/`, `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Investor art (or a documented pending-art entry).
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — free re-roll, relevance bias, movement cost.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table row + ability cell.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue row.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — catalog baselines.
- `tests/main-street/` — new `investor-staff.test.ts` (free re-roll, bias, movement) plus updates to `refresh-market.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `meta-progression.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `action-economy.test.ts` and any staff-count assertions.

## Related work

See **Related work (automated report)** below, plus manually identified items:

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open): escalates the paid re-roll cost; its appendix explicitly leaves "free re-rolls do not advance the escalation counter" as an assumption to settle with this item.
- `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` — "Rename the reroll button 'Research'" (in-progress): touches the same market re-roll button/tooltip; coordinate wording and the free-re-roll affordance.
- `MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0` — "Some staff cards should add action points" (completed): establishes the weekly action budget and the staff card UI/action patterns the movement cost builds on.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): most recent end-to-end staff-ability implementation (CSV → engine → docs → tests); follow its structure.
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — "Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card" (open): owns the art-less baseline; the Investor raises the drift-guard question.
- `MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL` — "Add a charity shop" (completed): precedent for adding a card and updating the catalog/count baselines.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Decision (free = coins-free, escalation-advancing):** because market re-roll is already action-free, "free re-roll, without using an action" means **no coin cost and no action cost**, but the free re-roll **advances** the per-turn escalation counter. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias definition):** "relevant to the type of business they are currently located at" = shares a synergy type with the hosting business; businesses/community-space by `synergyTypes`, events by `targetSynergy`, staff by `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias application):** the 75% applies per drawn slot with a random fallback; the entire row is not a single 75% roll. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (no stacking):** multiple Investors still grant a single free re-roll per turn (avoids a degenerate multi-Investor loop). *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (movement scope):** **all** staff relocation costs an action; the initial placement at hire time is unchanged. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Risk (scope creep / existing behaviour):** the re-roll cost item and the rename item touch the same button; implementing the free re-roll without advancing the counter would desynchronise the displayed price, and newly action-gating **all** staff relocation changes an existing free operation (and its tests). Mitigation: keep `refreshMarketCost()` authoritative, increment the shared counter on the free re-roll, and update the staff-placement tests in the same change.
- **Risk (determinism/tests):** adding a card changes seeded deck draws and several fixed-count baselines; many fixtures inline counts. Mitigation: update the documented baselines and count assertions in the same change, and cover the bias with a seeded-RNG test.
- **Risk (art drift guard):** a new art-less card fails `card-art.test.ts`; either supply a sprite or get a producer-approved pending-art entry, otherwise the item is blocked by `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`.
- **Risk (save compat):** forgetting the migrate backfill leaves old saves with `undefined` and a throwing/NaN free-re-roll gate. Mitigation: backfill in `migrateSerializedState` and assert a round-trip.
- **Risk (balance):** a free re-roll per turn plus a 75% biased row is a strong information advantage; cost/tier may need balancing (`balancing-methodology.md`). Mitigation: pick a mid/premium tier and revisit after playtest.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Round 1 (route: herdr auto-dispatch, 2026-09-30; answered by the producer 2026-09-30).**

- **Q1 (free re-roll semantics):** "The market re-roll is already action-free, so what does the Investor's 'free re-roll' free you from, and does it stack/interact with the escalating cost (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`)? Options: (a) one **coin-free** re-roll per turn, does **not** advance the escalation counter, multiple Investors do **not** stack; (b) one coin-free re-roll per Investor (stacks); (c) the free re-roll also resets the escalation counter; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** one coin-free, action-free re-roll per turn; it **does advance the escalation counter**; multiple Investors do **not** stack.

- **Q2 (relevance definition & application):** "How is 'relevant to the type of business they are currently located at' defined, and how does the 75% apply? Options: (a) a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`, event `targetSynergy`, staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap), applied **per drawn slot** with random fallback; (b) relevant by exact business name only; (c) the **whole row** is 75% likely to be relevant; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** as recommended — **(a)** shared synergy type, applied per drawn slot, with random fallback.

- **Q3 (movement cost & scope):** "Staff placement is action-free today. Should the Investor's move cost an action point, and does that apply to all staff? Options: (a) **Investor only** pays 1 action to relocate; other staff stay free; (b) **all staff** relocation costs 1 action; (c) the move is free but limited to once per turn; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** **(b)** — **all** staff relocation costs 1 action.

**Secondary assumptions (not asked in Round 1, to keep to the ≤3-question limit):**

- **Card economics (default):** `staff-investor` is a generalist (all synergy types), `handSlotsAdded: 0`, tier 5, cost 1000, ongoing 125 — mirroring the tier-5 specialist band (Financial Advisor). *Recorded as an assumption; the producer may re-balance.*
- **Art (default):** add a dedicated 1024×1024 Investor sprite and regenerate `card-art-map.json`; if art cannot be produced, request a producer-approved pending-art entry so the drift guard passes.
- **Rename coordination (default):** implement the free-re-roll affordance on the existing re-roll button so it survives the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename without conflicting wording.

**Research finding (agent, 2026-09-30):** The free re-roll and relevance bias are **not** implemented anywhere (repo + worklog search). The re-roll is already action-free and coin-costed (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`); `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) is the single composition point; staff placement is action-free (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`). This item is therefore a **new mechanic + card + docs + art** change, not a data-only change.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ** – Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution (open)
- **MS-0MUE2U21C0007BKL** – [test-failure] upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts > animates the transfer from the drop location and plays the upgrade SFX (beginDrag timeout) — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ability, ac4, ac5, acceptance, action (+430 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: abilities, ability, acceptance, action, add (+332 more)

# Problem statement

The contextual first-bank hint overlay (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) fires during the tutorial when the player ends a turn with spare actions, creating a "dead end" that interrupts tutorial progression and confuses the tutorial state machine. The hint is designed for normal gameplay and should not fire while the tutorial is active.

## Users

- **New players** completing the Main Street tutorial — they expect a linear, guided experience. An unexpected banking hint overlay mid-tutorial interrupts this flow, potentially showing a stale or completed tutorial step after the hint is dismissed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Banking hint does not fire during tutorial:** The contextual first-bank hint trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` must check that `tutorialController.isActive` is `false` (i.e., the tutorial is not active). The hint must never fire while the tutorial overlay is showing or a tutorial step is pending.
2. **Banking hint fires in normal gameplay:** The hint continues to fire exactly once when a non-tutorial player ends a turn with `actionsRemaining > 0`, respecting the persistence flag (`hasSeenBankingHint`).
3. **No regression to tutorial flow:** Existing tutorial steps, overlay lifecycle, and step progression remain unchanged. The tutorial still completes through all 26 steps without interruption from the banking hint.
4. **No regression to banking hint:** The hint still triggers correctly in normal gameplay after the tutorial is complete (on the first end-turn with spare actions).
5. **All tests pass:** Existing tutorial unit and browser tests pass; no new failures introduced.

## Constraints

- **Minimal change:** Only the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` needs modification (one logical operator change). No new fields, no structural changes.
- **Tutorial-layer only:** The fix is entirely within Main Street's tutorial wiring; no core-engine, card-system, or UI component changes.
- **Existing banking hint implementation preserved:** The `BANKING_HINT_STEP`, `renderBankingHint()`, and `TutorialState` banking hint flag remain unchanged.

## Existing state

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** implemented the contextual first-bank hint with the following trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`:
  ```ts
  if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0) {
      pendingBankingHint = true;
      // persist flag via TutorialState
  }
  ```
- This condition fires when the tutorial is **active** AND the player has spare actions.
- The `renderBankingHint()` method saves the current tutorial step, shows the banking hint overlay, and on dismiss tries to restore the saved step — but if the tutorial step has already advanced (e.g., T6 End Turn completed), the restoration shows a stale step, creating the "dead end."
- The intent from the original brief (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) was that the hint fires **once per save** on the first bankable end-turn — but the implementation does not distinguish between tutorial and normal gameplay contexts.

## Desired change

Change the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` from:
```ts
if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```
to:
```ts
if (!tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```

This ensures the banking hint only fires in normal gameplay (after the tutorial is complete), never during the tutorial.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — One-line fix: invert the `tut?.isActive` check in the banking hint trigger (endTurn path, ~line 221).

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (completed, merged) — Main Street: tutorial coverage for action banking (parent feature that introduced the contextual first-bank hint).
- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed, merged) — Main Street: action banking (engine-level banking logic).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** If the producer believes the banking hint should also fire during the tutorial (e.g., as an optional teaching moment), that would require a different design — but the title and description indicate this is clearly unintended.
- **No edge cases:** The banking hint has a one-shot persistence flag; if the hint never fires during the tutorial (which is the fix), it will fire on the player's first non-tutorial end-turn with spare actions — this is the intended behaviour.

# Write storylines — harden, document, and extend the Main Street storyline system

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-09-26): **Q1 = epic**; **Q2 = implement all
improvements now**; **Q3 = keep Main Street-specific, but design with an eye to
extracting into core-engine in future — cutting corners is acceptable now, but
do not make extraction impossible.**

## Problem statement

Main Street has a *rough* storyline implementation: incident event cards can
carry a dual choice (`hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId`)
and the player's Accept/Reject decision schedules the next card in a chain
(`CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128`). The mechanic works and is tested, but it is thin,
implicit, and undocumented:

- the branching model supports only binary choices with one successor per
  branch, with no storyline identity/grouping;
- there is no static validation — a dangling chain link is only logged at
  runtime (`Chain card X not found in card data.`);
- there is no authoring, validation, or visualisation tooling (chains are
  hand-edited inside a 155-row CSV);
- no documentation explains how storylines are created and managed; and
- storylines are invisible to players as stories — they see two opaque
  buttons and no memory of how their choices shaped events.

This makes storylines hard to extend safely and invisible as a source of
player agency.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — author, extend and balance storylines
  (new chains, retro-fitting existing incidents) without editing engine code,
  and see the shape of a storyline at a glance.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need a documented, validated, and
  flexible data model with clear seams so storyline changes cannot silently
  break, and so the mechanic can later move to the core engine.
- **Players** — should feel their choices shape an unfolding story, with
  visible continuity (what they chose, what it led to, which thread is still
  running) rather than two opaque buttons.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — need a decision policy that remains correct as the
  branching model and option counts grow.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to define a storyline declaratively and run a
  validator, so I know every branch resolves before I ship it."
- "As a developer, I want a documented storyline model and an authoring guide,
  so I can add a multi-step chain without reverse-engineering the engine."
- "As a player, I want a storyline journal that shows my past choices and what
  they led to, so my decisions feel like they build a narrative."
- "As a player, I want to know which story threads are still running, so
  recurring events feel connected rather than random."
- "As a producer, I want a prioritised roadmap of further storyline
  improvements, so I can schedule the next iteration."

## Scope areas (all to be implemented — Q2 = all now)

### A. Model & engine hardening (+ future extraction seam)

1. **Storyline identity/grouping** — optional `storylineId` (+ display
   `storylineTitle`) on `EventCard` and in the CSV, grouping chain cards into
   named storylines. Backward compatible.
2. **Generalised option model** — support an ordered list of options (each
   with a label, a successor card id, and an effect policy of apply/skip),
   while preserving legacy `hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` /
   `rejectNextCardId` semantics byte-for-byte.
3. **Extraction seam** — isolate storyline definitions, state and resolution
   behind a small game-agnostic interface/registry and pure functions, with
   migration notes, so the mechanic can move to `src/core-engine` later
   without rewriting callers. Corners may be cut, but the boundary must exist
   and be documented.
4. **Static validation** — every link resolves; no dangling, duplicate or
   unknown references; sinks and cycles are intentional. Validation fails
   loudly (non-zero exit), not just via a runtime log.
5. **Invariants preserved** — undo/redo, save/load (old saves load), deferred
   end-of-turn mutation, transcript shape and AI resolution stay correct for
   all option counts.

### B. Documentation

6. Canonical **`docs/main-street/storylines.md`**: concepts, data model + CSV
   columns, resolution lifecycle, AI policy, tooling usage, an end-to-end
   authoring walkthrough with a worked example, an authoring checklist, and a
   documented extraction path to core-engine.
7. **`docs/DEVELOPER.md`** and **`example-games/main-street/README.md`**
   cross-reference the doc and list the new CSV columns and scripts.
8. A **doc-drift test** asserts the docs exist and that documented chain
   examples match the shipped CSV.
9. A prioritised **future-improvements roadmap** (tooling + player agency)
   documenting anything deliberately deferred, with deferred ideas captured as
   work items.

### C. Tooling (implemented)

10. **Validator** — `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` + an npm script
    (`validate:storylines`), wired into the test suite / pre-push so
    regressions fail the build.
11. **Graph / manifest export** — tool to emit a storyline graph or manifest
    (`--format mermaid|json`) plus a committed generated artefact and a JSON
    schema.
12. **Authoring helper** — a CLI (or equivalent documented commands) to add and
    link storyline cards safely, without hand-editing CSV internals.

### D. Player agency (implemented)

13. **Named storylines surfaced** in the choice dialog and activity log.
14. **Storyline journal/history overlay** — review past choices and outcomes,
    accessible from the HUD, using the standard overlay pattern and
    reduced-motion behaviour, backed by the existing transcript/log.
15. **Choice clarity** — explanatory tooltips/labels for each option that
    explain consequence semantics **without** revealing the escalation card
    (preserving the designed tension).
16. **Outcome feedback** — each resolved choice produces a concise narrative
    "story update" line tied to its `storylineId`.
17. **Continuity / foreshadowing** — an active/recurring-thread indicator while
    a storyline is in play (including cycles).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storyline metadata** — `EventCard` (and the CSV) supports an optional
   `storylineId` and `storylineTitle`; the parser populates them; cards
   without them behave exactly as before. Covered by unit tests.
2. **Generalised option model** — the engine supports an arbitrary ordered
   list of options (label, successor card id, effect policy apply/skip);
   legacy `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` cards resolve
   identically. Covered by unit tests proving legacy-equivalence and a
   multi-option resolution.
3. **Extraction seam** — storyline definition/state/resolution are behind a
   documented game-agnostic interface/registry boundary with pure functions
   and explicit migration notes in the docs; no caller reaches into
   Main-Street-only internals for resolution.
4. **Static validation passes** — every `acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId`
   (and any new option link) in `card-data.csv` resolves to an existing card;
   no dangling/duplicate/unknown references; validation exits non-zero on
   failure and is enforced in the test suite or pre-push hook.
5. **Invariants preserved** — undo/redo, save/load (old saves without new
   fields load), deferred end-of-turn mutation, transcript `event-choice`
   records, and AI resolution remain correct for all option counts; covered by
   unit tests.

6. **Canonical documentation** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` exists and
   documents concepts, the data model and CSV columns, the resolution
   lifecycle (deferred `pendingEventChoice`, option paths, deck insertion,
   undo/redo, save/load, transcript), the AI policy, tooling usage, a
   step-by-step authoring walkthrough with a worked example, an authoring
   checklist, and the core-engine extraction path.
7. **Cross-references updated** — `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and
   `example-games/main-street/README.md` reference the new doc and list the new
   CSV columns and scripts.
8. **Doc-drift guard** — at least one test/lint asserts the canonical doc
   exists and that its documented chain examples match the shipped CSV.
9. **Future-improvements roadmap** — the documentation contains a prioritised
   roadmap of further tooling and player-agency improvements, and any deferred
   ideas are captured as separate work items.

10. **Validator script** — `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` plus an npm script
    (`validate:storylines`), returning non-zero on invalid storylines and
    covered by tests against both valid and deliberately broken fixtures.
11. **Graph/manifest export** — a tool emits the storyline graph/manifest
    (`--format mermaid|json`); a generated artefact and JSON schema are
    committed, and a test asserts the emitted graph matches the CSV.
12. **Authoring helper** — a documented CLI (or equivalent) can add a
    storyline card/link safely and validate the result; the workflow is covered
    by the authoring guide and at least one test.

13. **Named storylines surfaced** — the choice dialog and activity log show the
    storyline name (e.g. "Tax Troubles — …") when available, with a
    reduced-motion-safe presentation.
14. **Journal/history overlay** — a player can open a storyline journal from
    the HUD that lists past choices and their outcomes; it uses
    `createOverlayBackground`/`createOverlayButton`, parents elements into
    `hudContainer`, and is covered by a browser test.
15. **Choice clarity** — option buttons carry tooltips/labels explaining
    consequence semantics without revealing the escalation card; covered by a
    test.
16. **Outcome feedback** — each resolved choice emits a concise narrative
    "story update" line tied to its storyline; covered by a unit test.
17. **Continuity indicator** — an active/recurring-storyline indicator is
    visible while a storyline is in play and cleared when it ends; covered by a
    test.

18. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
    code comments, `README`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
19. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility** — cards without storyline fields behave exactly
  as before; existing `hasChoices` cards are unchanged; old saves load with
  missing fields defaulted.
- **Determinism / replay safety** — storyline resolution and chain-card
  insertion must not consume RNG or wall-clock time; transcripts stay
  replayable and deterministic.
- **No cost model change** — event choices remain free (no daily-action cost).
- **Preserve designed tension** — choice clarity must not preview the
  escalation card; the "unknown consequence" tension is intentional.
- **Extraction seam, not extraction** — the mechanic stays Main Street-specific
  for now; corners may be cut but the boundaries must not make a later move to
  `src/core-engine` a rewrite.
- **Existing event-flow decisions preserved** — deferred end-of-turn mutation,
  undo/redo semantics, AI difficulty policy and tutorial exclusion of choice

- **No new runtime dependency** beyond the existing Node/Vitest/scripts

# Add per-turn running costs to Playground, Town Fountain and Community Shelter

## Summary

Give the three remaining free-to-run Main Street community-space cards a per-turn running cost, following the Park precedent (CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK) and the producer decision of 2026-09-29. Today the Playground (`cs-playground`), Town Fountain (`cs-fountain`) and Community Shelter (`cs-shelter`) have `ongoingCost` empty → 0, so they are free synergy/reputation anchors.

## Problem statement

The Park was given a 40 coins/turn running cost to stop costless synergy spam. Three other community spaces still have no ongoing cost, so the same "free anchor" dynamic remains for their synergies:

- **Playground** (`cs-playground`) — cost 400, Entertainment, +5 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Town Fountain** (`cs-fountain`) — cost 500, Culture, +10 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Community Shelter** (`cs-shelter`) — cost 600, Service, +15 rep/turn, ongoing 0 (retiered T6→T3, CG-0MT5VZJLS000B8KI).

## Users

- **Player** — building a Playground/Fountain/Shelter cluster should feel the per-turn drain as a real strategic cost.
- **Producer / balance owner** — wants a running-cost lever on every community space, not just Park/Library/Garden/Kiosk/Public Art.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-playground`, `cs-fountain` and `cs-shelter` in the Main Street `card-data.csv` each have a non-zero integer `ongoingCost`, confirmed with the producer before merge. **Proposed mapping (agent suggestion, producer-owned — confirm or override): Playground 20, Town Fountain 25, Community Shelter 30.**
2. **Descriptions** — each updated `card-data.csv` description states the running cost using the existing wording ("Costs N coins per turn to run."), consistent with Library/Community Garden/Park, and the `card-text-data-consistency` test passes.
3. **Deduction** — at end of turn each placed, unsold card deducts its `ongoingCost` through the existing `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` path, clamped at 0 coins and logged with an insufficient-funds log when applicable.
4. **Tooltips** — each card's community-space tooltip shows `Ongoing cost: -N/turn`; each card's cash line shows `-N`.
5. **Sold-card exemption preserved** — a sold Playground/Fountain/Shelter incurs no ongoing cost (CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA).
6. **Tests** — add distinct coverage for each card's deduction, clamping and sold-exemption (no redundant duplicates); update every test that assumes these cards are free to run, specifically:
   - `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — "does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards" uses Playground + Fountain + Shelter; re-point at cards that remain free, or rework with synthetic zero-cost card fixtures.
   - `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — "should do nothing when no community space has an ongoing cost" places a Playground; rework with a synthetic zero-cost community-space fixture.
   - `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts` — "community space card with zero ongoingCost shows \"Ongoing cost: -0/turn\"" selects `find(c => c.ongoingCost === 0)`; after this change **no shipped community space has a zero `ongoingCost`**, so it must use a synthetic zero-cost card (business/staff variants already exist).
7. **Balance sanity** — Monte Carlo and tutorial guardrails remain green; any drift is measured and reported, and no guardrail band is silently widened. The tutorial scenario places no Playground/Fountain/Shelter (verified: tutorial uses Laundromat, Local Festival, Bookshop and Library only).
8. **Docs** — update `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (Ongoing/turn column), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` (special-cases) and any other doc listing these cards' running costs.
9. **Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** coins are whole integers (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); no fractional `ongoingCost`.
- **Data is source of truth:** the running cost lives in `card-data.csv`; tooltip, overlay and deduction derive from it.
- **Charging semantics unchanged:** placed, unsold cards only; clamped at 0; reuse the existing community-space mechanism.
- **Balance values are producer-owned:** the proposed mapping is an agent suggestion; the producer confirms or overrides before merge.
- **Zero-cost coverage must be synthetic:** after this change all eight shipped community spaces carry a non-zero `ongoingCost`, so tests of the "no ongoing cost" path can no longer rely on a shipped card.

## Existing state

- `cs-playground`: cost 400, baseIncome 0, Entertainment, rep 5, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-fountain`: cost 500, baseIncome 0, Culture, rep 10, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-shelter`: cost 600, baseIncome 0, Service, rep 15, `ongoingCost` empty.
- Other community spaces already charged: Park 40, Library 25, Community Garden 10, Health Kiosk 15, Public Art 25.
- Park precedent: commit `5ffd54a` in `tce-main-street` set `cs-park` to 40/turn and updated tests/tooltip/cash-line/docs.
- Tests that assume these cards are free: `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` ("does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards"); `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` ("should do nothing when no community space has an ongoing cost"); `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts` (`find(c => c.ongoingCost === 0)`).

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — set the three `ongoingCost` values and descriptions.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated by the suite; no SVG face change expected (community-space ongoing cost is not baked in).
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — add per-card deduction/clamp/sold coverage; rework the Playground zero-cost test.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — tooltip/cash-line coverage; rework zero-cost selection.
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — rework the zero-cost test.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`.

## Related work

- **CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK** — Park running cost 40/turn (precedent; producer confirmed the integer-economy mapping).
- CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 — integer economy ×100 rescale.
- CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA — sold cards excluded from ongoing costs.
- CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE — community-space ongoing-cost / Park-model synergy.
- CG-0MSQJ210I00491ZZ — Group B community-space expansion (added these three cards).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Value assumption:** the three proposed values (20/25/30) are an agent suggestion; the producer must confirm or override before merge.
- **Balance drift:** these cards appear in Monte Carlo simulations; run the guardrails and report drift rather than widening bands.
- **Test coupling:** three existing tests rely on these exact cards (or on any zero-cost community space) being free; all must be updated/reworked (expected, not a regression). After the change no shipped community space has `ongoingCost === 0`.
- **Scope creep:** additional community-space levers (e.g. adjusting Park/Library values) are out of scope; record them as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The proposed `ongoingCost` values are Playground 20, Town Fountain 25, Community Shelter 30 (agent suggestion). Confirm these, or provide override values? — **Recommended:** accept 20 / 25 / 30 — it establishes a rising `ongoingCost` gradient (20/25/30) across the three cards while keeping them below the existing Park (40) and in the same band as Library (25) / Public Art (25). Answer: (pending producer). Source: producer decision required before merge (AC1); values are producer-owned balance data.
- **Q:** Are the three cards a single item or separate? — **Recommended:** single item — the change is one uniform data/description/edit sweep across three cards, sharing tests, docs and a single producer value decision. Answer: (agent, from seed context) single item. Source: work-item seed context.

# Intake Brief: Easy editing of tutorial text

**Recreated from the core work item `CG-0MUAVHX1D002J8HH`** in the Tableau-Card-Engine store. The Main Street game — and therefore all tutorial copy — now lives in this repository (`tce-main-street`), so this item is the game-repo record of the same change. Cross-repo pointer: `CG-0MUAVHX1D002J8HH`; implementation commit `beeed4d` on `dev`.

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature**

## Problem statement

Main Street tutorial copy is already externalised out of gameplay code, but it lives in a **TypeScript source module** (`src/i18n/tutorial-en.ts`) whose values are wrapped in `tutorialKey(...)` / `modalKey(...)` / `overlayKey(...)` / `bankingHintKey(...)` expressions. Editing wording therefore requires opening a `.ts` file, understanding the key syntax, and risking a compile error — which is a barrier for the non-developer content/editorial writer who owns the copy. The producer wants all tutorial copy in a **CSV file that can be opened and edited in a spreadsheet**.

## Users

- **Non-developer content/editorial writer** — owns tutorial wording; must be able to edit it in a spreadsheet without touching TypeScript.
- **Developer/maintainer** — must be able to trust that a spreadsheet save cannot silently break the tutorial (missing/orphan/duplicate keys, mangled quoting, dropped placeholders).
- **Player** — must see the same (correct, data-driven) tutorial copy as today; this change is behaviour-preserving.

### Example user stories

- As a content editor, I want to open one CSV, edit the `text` column in my spreadsheet, save it, and have the tutorial use my wording after the normal build, so that I never need to understand TypeScript.
- As a developer, I want a build-time/CI test that validates the CSV (keys, duplicates, placeholders, quoting) so that a bad spreadsheet save cannot ship broken tutorial copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CSV is the single source of tutorial copy.** All tutorial strings — 26 step titles + 26 step bodies (`tutorial.T1..T26.title|body`), 4 offer-modal strings (`tutorial.modal.*`), 4 overlay button labels (`tutorial.overlay.*`), and 2 banking-hint strings (`tutorial.bankingHint.*`) — live in `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` with a `key,text` header. No user-facing prose string literals remain in `tutorial-en.ts` (it holds only key helpers + the loader). *Metric: a test asserts `tutorial-en.csv` has a `key,text` header and exactly the required keys; a grep/inspection confirms `tutorial-en.ts` contains no copy.*
2. **Loader preserves the public API.** `tutorial-en.ts` keeps exporting `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE`, `TUTORIAL_I18N_KEY_PREFIX`, `tutorialKey`, `modalKey`, `overlayKey`, and `bankingHintKey`, and builds `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE` from the CSV via a Vite `?raw` import + the core `parseCsv()` helper. All existing consumers (`src/TutorialFlow.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`, tests) compile and pass **unchanged**. *Metric: existing `tutorial-i18n.test.ts`, `tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`, `tutorial-flow.test.ts` pass without edits.*
3. **CSV integrity is validated.** A test verifies: header is `key,text`; every required key is present; there are no duplicate or orphan/unknown keys; no value is empty; embedded commas round-trip; the embedded double quote in the banking hint (`"(1 banked)"`) round-trips; a leading UTF-8 BOM is tolerated (the loader strips it); and placeholder tokens (`{cardName}`, `{cost}`, `{bonus}`, `{synergyCardName}`) are preserved where expected. *Metric: `tests/main-street/tutorial-csv.test.ts` all green.*
4. **Behaviour is preserved end-to-end.** `resolveTutorialStepText()` and `t()` resolve the same content as before the migration for every step (including data-driven card facts from `card-data.csv` and the modal/overlay/banking labels), with no raw `{token}` text leaking. *Metric: existing content assertions plus a full required-key parity assertion pass.*
5. **Documentation reflects the spreadsheet workflow.** `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` is updated so "Changing existing text" and "Adding a New Language" describe opening `tutorial-en.csv` in a spreadsheet, editing the `text` column, saving as CSV UTF-8 (quoting for embedded commas/quotes; keep placeholder tokens), and rebuilding. Any stale references to editing `tutorial-en.ts` are removed.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Bundle the CSV at build time via Vite `?raw` (no runtime `fetch`), matching `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts:13` (`./card-data.csv?raw`). A normal rebuild/redeploy is acceptable (producer Q3 = A).
- Use the existing core `parseCsv()` (`core/src/core-engine/CsvLoader.ts`, imported as `@core-engine/CsvLoader`) — no new runtime dependency. It already supports RFC4180 quoting: embedded commas, newlines, and escaped `""`.
- Preserve the i18n key scheme exactly (`tutorial.<STEP_ID>.<field>`, `tutorial.modal.*`, `tutorial.overlay.*`, `tutorial.bankingHint.*`).
- Preserve placeholder tokens `{cardName}` / `{cost}` / `{bonus}` / `{synergyCardName}`; card facts must keep resolving from `card-data.csv` at render time.
- Tolerate a UTF-8 BOM (`parseCsv` does not trim header cells, so the loader must strip it) and expect `parseCsv`'s value trimming.
- English only. No change to step order, gates, highlight zones, scenario, or gameplay logic.

## Existing state

- `src/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE: Record<string, string>` with inline strings plus key-helper functions and inline editorial comments.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts:88` — registers the bundle at module load (`registerLocale('en', TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE)`).
- `src/TutorialFlow.ts:68` — imports `bankingHintKey`/`tutorialKey`; steps carry only `titleKey`/`bodyKey`.
- `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` — already documents the i18n architecture and says to edit `tutorial-en.ts`.
- Precedent for spreadsheet-editable bundled data: `card-data.csv` parsed by `parseCsv()` (`src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`).
- Copy characteristics (measured at intake): 62 values; 13 contain commas; 1 contains an embedded double quote; none contain newlines.

## Desired change

Introduce `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` (`key,text`) holding all tutorial strings, and reduce `src/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` to a thin loader that imports the CSV `?raw`, parses it with `parseCsv()`, strips an optional BOM, and exports the same `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE` plus key helpers. Add a CSV-integrity test and update the localization docs to describe the spreadsheet workflow.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` — **New.** `key,text` CSV holding all tutorial/modal/overlay/banking strings (spreadsheet-editable source of truth).
- `src/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Convert to a thin loader: `?raw` import + `parseCsv()` + BOM strip → `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE`; keep all existing exports.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-csv.test.ts` — **New.** CSV integrity: header, required-key completeness, duplicates/orphans, empty values, comma/quote round-trip, BOM tolerance, placeholder preservation.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-i18n.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-flow.test.ts` — Confirm still pass unchanged (behaviour-preservation evidence).
- `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` — Rewrite "Changing existing text" / "Adding a New Language" and the file-overview table for the CSV workflow.
- `docs/main-street/playtest-scenarios.md` — Update the tutorial-copy editing pointer.
- `core/src/core-engine/CsvLoader.ts` — Existing parser; use as-is (only touch if a proven gap, e.g. header trimming/BOM, is found).

## Related work

- **`CG-0MUAVHX1D002J8HH` — Easy editing of tutorial text (core store).** The originating item; this MS item mirrors it for the game repo that now owns the copy.
- **`MS-0MUN91YJ40092ZBM` — Steam follow CTA in the tutorial completion step** (open): later added the 5 `tutorial.steamFollow.*` keys to the CSV; the integrity test's required-key list grew from 62 to 67 accordingly.
- **`MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5` — Fix stale `example-games/main-street` paths in docs after the `src/` migration** (open): tracks the remaining stale path references in the localization docs.
- **`CG-0MP415DUV0032SKK` — Main Street tutorial localization and i18n externalization** (completed): externalised copy into the i18n bundle this item now moves to CSV.
- **`CG-0MS0IXWE2002ZQ16` / `CG-0MSBSCL0W005OALV` — Data-driven tutorial text** (completed): added `{cardName}`/`{cost}`/`{bonus}` placeholder resolution from `card-data.csv`; the CSV must preserve these tokens.
- **`CG-0MSBSCCPJ0050DT4` — Core i18n interpolation support** (completed): `t(key, params)` used during resolution.
- **`CG-0MSBSCRND009V8DS` / `CG-0MSLXJ1OK004LJKU` — Tutorial localization docs** (completed): docs this change revised again.
- **`CG-0MQK3IYDT0024SWG` — Tutorial text needs review on Main Street** (completed): editorial rules the CSV must continue to satisfy.
- **`CG-0MQF4A8QZ008NLWM` — Tests: Tutorial text updates** (completed): test suite guarding tutorial text content.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Spreadsheet round-trip mangling** (re-quoting, encoding, BOM, header changes) → mitigation: RFC4180 quoting is already supported; integrity test + BOM strip; docs instruct "Save As CSV (UTF-8)".
- **Silent key loss during migration** → mitigation: required-key parity test and unchanged existing content tests.
- **In-file editorial comments lost** in the move to CSV → mitigation: editorial rules live in `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` and the loader's module comment (an optional `notes` column could be added later if writers want inline guidance).
- **`parseCsv` trims values and does not trim header cells** → assume no copy relies on leading/trailing whitespace (true at intake) and strip the BOM in the loader.
- **Scope creep** → do **not** extend this to `undo-challenge-en.ts`, add new locales, or build an in-game editor; record those as separate future work items.
- **Assumption:** a 2-column `key,text` layout is acceptable (a `notes`/`step` column can be added later without breaking the loader).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** — "Is the existing `tutorial-en.ts` i18n bundle sufficient as the 'config file', or must copy move to a standalone data/config file?" (options: A close as satisfied / B standalone data file / C keep TS + tooling only). **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-26): "No not sufficient, we should use a CSV file that is editable in a spreadsheet."** → Chosen: **B**, CSV format.
- **Q2** — "Who is the intended editor of the tutorial text?" (A developer / B non-developer writer / C translator). **Answer (producer): "b (but does it matter?)"** → Non-developer content/editorial writer.
- **Q3** — "Does 'easy' require only no-code editing, or also no rebuild?" (A no-code + rebuild / B runtime fetch, no rebuild). **Answer (producer): "A"** → No-code editing plus a normal build/redeploy; the CSV is bundled via Vite `?raw`.

As a Main Street player or observer, I want to watch AI-vs-AI competitive matches with spectator/replay visuals, so that I can study the AI strategies and enjoy demos without taking a turn.

## Background

- Discovered from epic **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** (Playable AI competitive mode). That epic covers the human-vs-AI playable mode; this item adds the all-AI observer experience on top and is **not** a dependency of the epic.

5. **No regressions.** Single-player and the human-vs-AI competitive mode are unaffected. *Metric: existing unit/integration tests pass.*

- Rendering/visual items may require manual verification; keep the deterministic-replay AC automated.
- Reuse the transcript/seed determinism already required by the engine rather than adding a parallel recording mechanism.

# Intake Brief: Avoid duplicate Main Street card SVG regeneration on game start (MS-0MUTU19SF007791K)

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Bug** | **Assignee: Map**

> Main Street regenerates all 174 card SVGs from CSV data twice on every game start, because `loadCampaignAndSetup()` regenerates synchronously and then regenerates again after the async static-SVG fetches resolve. The duplicate work wastes startup CPU and emits a misleading duplicate console log.

## Problem Statement

When a Main Street game starts, `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` runs twice, producing the duplicate console line:

```
MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts:112 [MainStreetSvgTextureManager] Regenerated 174 card SVGs from CSV data
MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts:112 [MainStreetSvgTextureManager] Regenerated 174 card SVGs from CSV data
```

The second regeneration exists as a defensive re-apply: `loadCardSvgSources()` (called from `preload()`) starts async `fetch()`es for the static SVG assets, and those fetch callbacks call `cardSvgSources.set(...)` unconditionally, so a late-resolving fetch can clobber the CSV-fresh SVG that the synchronous regeneration just produced. To defeat that race, `loadCampaignAndSetup()` chains a second `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` onto `cardSvgLoadPromise`.

That is correct but wasteful: the whole 174-row `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow()` pass (including embedded base64 card art) runs twice on every boot, and the duplicate log makes it look like the startup pipeline is broken. The same redundancy is latent in `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()`, which regenerates a third time whenever a CSV mismatch is detected — even though the synchronous early regeneration has already made the sources fresh.

## Users

- **Developer:** Starting the dev server and reading the browser console. A duplicate "Regenerated 174 card SVGs" line is confusing and suggests the CSV/SVG startup pipeline is firing twice.
  - *"As a developer, I want the startup log to clearly show one regeneration, so I can trust that the CSV→SVG pipeline runs once and is not double-initialised."*
- **Player (startup latency):** Card SVG generation is on the boot critical path. Doing it twice adds avoidable work before the first frame renders.
  - *"As a player, I want the game to start as quickly as possible and not do redundant work while loading."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Single regeneration per CSV content per manager:** `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` is idempotent for an unchanged `CSV_CHECKSUM` — calling it twice in a row generates the CSV SVGs once, logs the "Regenerated … card SVGs" message once, and the second call is a cheap no-op. Verified by a unit test that spies on the generation pass / log and asserts one run.
2. **Fetched static SVGs never clobber CSV-fresh sources:** `loadCardSvgSources()` does not overwrite a `cardSvgSources` entry that is already populated, so a late-resolving static-SVG `fetch()` cannot replace a CSV-regenerated source. Verified by a unit test with a mocked `fetch` that pre-populates a template id and asserts it is unchanged after the fetch resolves.
3. **No regression in CSV freshness:** After the async `cardSvgLoadPromise` chain completes on a boot with unchanged CSV, every template id present in the CSV still maps to the CSV-generated SVG (not the static asset) and the non-CSV card-back template remains populated. Verified by an existing/added test.
4. **Redundant re-apply chain removed:** `loadCampaignAndSetup()` no longer performs a second `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` after `cardSvgLoadPromise`; the synchronous early regeneration remains, and prewarming is still guaranteed to run after a fresh regeneration. Verified by code inspection + the no-console-errors E2E remains green.
5. **Mismatch path is non-redundant:** When `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()` runs against sources already regenerated for the current `CSV_CHECKSUM`, it does not trigger another full generation pass.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments (the JSDoc in `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` and the comments in `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts`), README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve the CSV-freshness guarantee:** the fix must not reintroduce the race fixed by `CG-0MRH36Z6800065JC` (stale static SVGs winning over CSV data).
- **Keep the synchronous early regeneration:** it populates `cardSvgSources` before the async fetches resolve, so the first synchronous `refreshAll()` renders CSV-fresh cards rather than fallback placeholders. Removing it would regress first paint.
- **No new dependencies / no build-pipeline change:** work within the existing Vite + Phaser setup.
- **Game repo only:** this is a Main Street change (`tce-main-street`); no core-engine API changes are expected.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` loops `getCsvRows()` and calls `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow(row)` for each row, storing results in `scene.cardSvgSources` and logging on success.
- `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.loadCardSvgSources()` fetches static SVGs (one per template id + the card back) and sets `cardSvgSources` unconditionally in each `.then()` callback.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.loadCampaignAndSetup()` calls `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` synchronously and then reassigns `s.cardSvgLoadPromise = s.cardSvgLoadPromise.then(() => regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv())` — the source of the duplicate.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()` may call `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` a third time.
- Existing unit tests in `tests/main-street/svg-texture-cache-invalidation.test.ts` cover regeneration + prewarm-at-DPR invalidation, but not idempotency or the fetch-overwrite guard.
- Background/design: `CG-0MRH36Z6800065JC` ("Ensure card data is loaded from CSV when a new game starts") introduced the synchronous early regeneration and documented the race; this item tidies the defensive double-regeneration it left behind.

## Desired Change

Make regeneration idempotent and remove the redundant re-apply:

1. **Track provenance for fetched vs regenerated sources.** In `loadCardSvgSources()`, only set a `cardSvgSources` entry when one is not already present (or otherwise record that CSV regeneration owns those keys), so static-SVG fetches can never overwrite CSV-fresh entries. The card-back template (not in the CSV) is still set by its fetch.
2. **Memoise CSV regeneration.** Record the `CSV_CHECKSUM` that `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` last generated for; a subsequent call with the same checksum returns early (no generation pass, no log). This makes the `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()` path a no-op when sources are already fresh, and makes "Reset All Progress" (`StatsOverlay` re-invokes `loadCampaignAndSetup()`) cheap.
3. **Remove the redundant re-apply chain** in `loadCampaignAndSetup()`; keep the synchronous early regeneration and the existing `cardSvgLoadPromise.then(prewarm…)` ordering so prewarming still only sees fresh sources.
4. Update the surrounding comments/JSDoc to describe the new single-regeneration contract.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — Add CSV-checksum memoisation to `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` and a no-overwrite guard to `loadCardSvgSources()`; update JSDoc.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts` — Remove the second `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` re-apply chain in `loadCampaignAndSetup()`; update comments.
- `tests/main-street/svg-texture-cache-invalidation.test.ts` — Add unit tests for regeneration idempotency and the fetch no-overwrite guard.
- `tests/e2e/main-street-no-console-errors.browser.test.ts` — Existing guard that the boot pipeline stays console-clean; keep green (no change expected).

## Related Work

- `CG-0MRH36Z6800065JC` — [Completed] "Ensure card data is loaded from CSV when a new game starts". Introduced the synchronous early regeneration and the race-avoidance design that this item simplifies.
- `CG-0MRF343AJ004N6ZW` — [Completed] "Ensure SVGs are regenerated when CSV changes on game start and load". Added the CSV checksum + regeneration pipeline.
- `CG-0MRBDPFPH009Y8M0` — Game balance tooling built on CSV-driven card data (consumes the same `cardSvgSources`/regeneration seam).
- `MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY` — Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift guard (doc-relevant).

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Stale-source regression:** if the no-overwrite guard is too broad, the card-back template or any template absent from the CSV could be left unpopulated. Mitigation: guard by presence of an existing entry only; do not filter by `ms_card_` prefix, and keep the guard template-agnostic so non-CSV assets still load.
- **Memoisation masking a legitimate re-generation.** If SVG generation ever becomes state-dependent (not purely CSV-derived), the checksum key would be insufficient. Mitigation: key the memo on `CSV_CHECKSUM` and document the invariant that generated SVGs are a pure function of the CSV.
- **Scene-restart map persistence:** `scene.cardSvgSources` is a scene-level `Map` that survives a scene restart; the memo lives on the (freshly constructed) manager. Mitigation: the synchronous regeneration still runs once per new manager and overwrites CSV keys, so restart remains correct.
- **Scope creep:** eliminating the static SVG fetch path entirely, or moving to runtime-only generation, is out of scope. Record such opportunities as linked work items.
- **Test brittleness:** asserting on `console.info` text is fragile. Prefer asserting on a spied generation call count / returned count, with the log check as a secondary assertion.

### Assumptions

- The two observed log lines come from the synchronous regeneration (`loadCampaignAndSetup`) plus the `cardSvgLoadPromise` re-apply, not from a second scene instance or the `StatsOverlay` "Reset All" path (that path is only reachable from the stats-confirm overlay).
- `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow()` output is a pure function of the CSV rows, so regeneration is safely memoised by `CSV_CHECKSUM`.
- The static SVGs are only a fallback for when CSV regeneration is unavailable/fails.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1: Is the duplicate regeneration a correctness bug or a performance/observability concern?**
  - Answer (operator, freeform seed): reported as a bug — the console output shows two identical regeneration lines. Analysis: the final rendered cards are correct (the defensive second pass wins); the impact is wasted startup work, a misleading log, and a fragile double-regeneration contract. Research: traced the two calls to `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.loadCampaignAndSetup()` (synchronous early call + `cardSvgLoadPromise` re-apply), with a latent third call in `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()`.
  - Final: treat as a medium-priority bug (redundant work + misleading observability), not a rendering-correctness failure.
- **Q2: Which repository/store should own this work?**
  - Answer (agent, per project multi-repo rules): the change is entirely within the sibling game repo `tce-main-street`, which has its own Worklog store (prefix `MS`), so the item is created there (`MS-0MUTU19SF007791K`). Historical related items live in the core `CG` store because Main Street was previously part of the core repo.
  - Final: Main Street store (`MS`).
- **Q3: Should the fix remove the static-SVG fetch path or just stop it clobbering regenerated sources?**
  - Answer (agent, scope control): out of scope. The minimal, robust change is to (a) prevent fetches from overwriting CSV-fresh entries and (b) memoise regeneration, leaving the static SVGs as the fallback path.
  - Final: keep the fetch/fallback path; only prevent overwrite and redundant regeneration.


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV** – Storyline model & extraction seam (completed)

# Cross-owner business actions: seats can sell/close/upgrade businesses they do not own

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, the human seat can open the Manage-Card
dialog on an AI-owned street slot and **sell** or **close** that opponent's
business; the same ownership gap lets the human **upgrade** an opponent's
business. Each seat must only be able to mutate street slots it owns, in both
directions (human→AI and, defensively, AI→human).

## Users

- **Human player (competitive mode)** — expects opponent businesses to be
  untouchable; the current behaviour lets them destroy an opponent's engine and
  (for a sell) even credits the acting seat's wallet.
- **AI opponents** — must be prevented from mutating the human's businesses;
  today they emit no sell/close actions, but no guard exists to stop a future
  AI upgrade/sell/close path from doing so.

Example user stories:

- As a competitive player, I want to be unable to sell or close a business I
  do not own, so that opponents' engines are protected and the game is fair.
- As a competitive player, I want clear feedback when I click a slot I do not
  own, so that I understand why the action is unavailable.
- As a game designer, I want ownership enforced in one legality layer, so that
  UI, AI, and headless paths cannot diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive mode, `canSellBusiness`/`sellBusiness` reject a slot whose
   owner (`getSlotOwnerId`) is not the acting seat (`state.activePlayerId`),
   returning a `LegalityResult` with a clear reason; the action mutates no
   state. Single-player (no `ownerTaggedGrid`) behaviour is unchanged.
2. In competitive mode, `canCloseBusiness`/`closeBusiness` reject a slot whose
   owner is not the acting seat with the same guarantees; a rejected close
   consumes no action.
3. In competitive mode, upgrade actions (`canPurchaseUpgrade`,
   `canPlayUpgradeFromHand`, and their execution paths) reject targeting an
   opponent-owned business; eligible-target search does not select an
   opponent-owned slot as the default target.
4. Clicking a non-owned occupied slot in the scene blocks the Manage-Card
   dialog and shows illegal-move feedback with an ownership-specific message
   (e.g. "That business belongs to AI 1."); no dialog is opened and no Sell /
   Close / upgrade command runs.
5. Any coins from a permitted sell are credited to the owning seat's wallet
   (not an unrelated seat), and a permitted close leaves the slot immediately
   placeable by its owner; both behaviours are covered by tests.
6. Tests cover: human cannot sell/close/upgrade an AI-owned business; a seat
   can sell/close its **own** business (positive case); single-player
   sell/close/upgrade is unaffected; and the legality helpers return the
   expected reasons.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Enforce at the legality/command layer** (operator decision Q3 = A), not the
  scene layer alone, so UI, AI and headless paths share one source of truth.
- **Preserve single-player behaviour**: single-player states have no
  `ownerTaggedGrid`; the gate must be a no-op there.
- **Reuse existing ownership primitives**: `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`), `ownerTaggedGrid`, `activePlayerId`.
- **No new scoring/economy rules**: this is an access-control fix, not a
  balance change.
- **Headless/Monte-Carlo determinism** must not change for existing seeds where
  neither seat acted cross-owner (the AI emits no such actions today).
- Do not weaken the existing phase, sold-slot, action-budget, or placement-mode
  gates already in `canSellBusiness`/`canCloseBusiness`.

## Existing state

- `canSellBusiness`, `sellBusiness`, `canCloseBusiness`, `closeBusiness`
  (`src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`) contain **no ownership check**.
- `sellBusiness` credits `state.resourceBank.coins` directly, with no per-owner
  routing.
- `onSellCard` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts`) opens the
  Manage-Card dialog for any occupied, non-sold slot in `market` phase.
- `showSellConfirmation` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`) wires Sell
  and Close buttons that execute with no ownership check.
- `canPurchaseUpgrade` / `canPlayUpgradeFromHand` / `purchaseUpgrade`
  (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) have no ownership check;
  `findTargetBusinessSlot` may resolve to an opponent-owned business.
- Ownership is modelled: `getSlotOwnerId`, `tagSlotOwnerIfCompetitive`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`), `ownerTaggedGrid`, `activePlayerId`,
  and `PlayerRecord.controller` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`).
- The AI action enumerator (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
  `enumerateLegalActions`) emits no sell/close actions today; competitive
  income/costs are already routed per owner via `getSlotOwnerId`.

## Desired change

- Add an ownership guard to the sell/close legality and execution functions:
  when `ownerTaggedGrid` is present, require
  `getSlotOwnerId(state, slotIndex) === (state.activePlayerId ?? 0)`; otherwise
  reject with a descriptive reason. Single-player remains a no-op.
- Apply the same guard to upgrade targeting (`canPurchaseUpgrade`,
  `canPlayUpgradeFromHand`, and execution), and ensure default target selection
  never picks an opponent-owned slot.
- Gate the scene path (`onSellCard`) and/or the overlay so a non-owned slot
  cannot open the Manage-Card dialog; show the ownership-specific illegal-move
  message instead.
- Ensure a permitted sell credits the owning seat's wallet (the acting seat is
  the owner once the guard is in place — verify no separate routing is needed).
- Add focused unit tests plus a browser/scene-level test for the blocked dialog.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts` — add ownership gate to `canSellBusiness`,
  `sellBusiness`, `canCloseBusiness`, `closeBusiness`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — add ownership gate to
  `canPurchaseUpgrade`, `canPlayUpgradeFromHand`, `purchaseUpgrade`; fix
  `findTargetBusinessSlot` default selection.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — reuse `getSlotOwnerId`; may add a small
  `canActOnOwner`/`isSlotOwnedByActiveSeat` helper.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — apply the same guard to the legacy
  `sellFromTableau` / `canSellFromTableau` path if still reachable.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts` — block `onSellCard` for
  non-owned slots with ownership feedback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — defensive guard in the Sell/Close
  handlers (and hide/disable when non-owned).
- `tests/main-street/CloseBusiness.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` — extend with ownership cases.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-*.test.ts` — add cross-owner sell/close/upgrade
  cases (a new `competitive-ownership-actions.test.ts` is likely cleanest).
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — blocked-dialog case.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W` — Reject illegal moves before animation and
  action-point deduction (completed; the established pattern for validating a
  move before any state mutation/animation — reuse it for the ownership gate).
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the
  shared street (epic, establishes `ownerTaggedGrid`).
- `MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP` — Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI).
- `MS-0MT5X3N79002S038` — Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware,
  staff-free scoring for shared-street play (ownership-aware AI logic).
- `MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY` — Competitive state model: per-player resources,
  owner-tagged street.
- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident
  resolution (precedent for per-owner routing).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** applying the gate too broadly breaks single-player or legacy saves
  (no `ownerTaggedGrid`). Mitigation: gate strictly on `ownerTaggedGrid`
  presence; add single-player regression tests.
- **Risk:** the AI's default upgrade target (`findTargetBusinessSlot`) changes
